text: {"frames":["Femke the silent ferrywoman stands on the barge with her blue lantern unlit, because the Tower has drawn her route in wet ink on the wall and the ice is coming. The route has three parts, 2 cells, then 4 cells, then 5 cells, and every cell is 5 m on the ground. She will not speak a word or light the lantern until she knows the length, so she hands you the chalk and waits by the rope. How many metres long is the route?","Every night at midnight the humming behind the cupboard in the lock house grows louder, and Thijs the old lock keeper follows it with a candle and a cheese knife. The tune leads through three stretches of canal: first 2 cells, then 4 cells, then 5 cells, and each cell is 5 m on the ground. Whenever he counts a step wrong, the humming stops and the cupboard door creaks shut. He whispers that you must count the cells with him, so he can tell the tune where to go. How many metres long is the route?","The faraway music rises through the floor of the cheese cellar, and the cheese maker Anneke sees that someone has painted the route on the wall wrongly. The three parts are 2 cells, 4 cells and 5 cells, and each cell is 5 m on the ground. The wheels of cheese will roll the wrong way until the wall is scraped and painted again. She holds out the brush to you and waits for the total. How many metres long is the route?","A smell of wet tar drifts up the stairs of the Tower, and Isa the cat is already counting the steps down to the lock. The water in the lock rises and falls as if it is breathing, and the gate will only swing open once the route is known. The route runs 2 cells, then 4 cells, then 5 cells, and every cell is 5 m on the ground. Isa's tail is twitching and the water is climbing the steps. How many metres long is the route?","Every window of the crooked house with the hoist beam glows gold, although nobody has lit a lamp inside. Luuk, the keeper of forgotten things, knows a trick when he sees one, because the glow wants him to leave his store unguarded. He stretches a paper rope between the beams and lays out the route: 2 cells, then 4 cells, then 5 cells, each cell 5 m on the ground. If he gets the length wrong, the windows will pull every forgotten thing out into the street. How many metres long is the route?"]}
